question.leadin: This man was born near Lake Baikal with the name Temujin ("TEH-moo-jin").
question.text: Name this man who was proclaimed "universal ruler" in a 1206 assembly.
question.clue: This ruler's general, Jebe, defeated the Kievan Rus at the Battle of the Kalka River.

swap.text: Kazakhstan has the longest coastline on this body of water which, despite its name, is the largest lake in the world. This lake also borders Russia, Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkmenistan, and caviar is often procured from fish in this lake.
swap.answerHtml: Caspian Sea [or Kaspii Tenizi, or Hazar Denzi, or Hezer Denizi]
swap.clue: The world's first oil tanker sailed across this body of water from a port that produced half of the world's oil in 1900.

question.leadin: This ruler defeated Tokhtamysh [TOKE-TAM-ISH] at the Battle of the Terek River. --.
question.text: Name this conqueror from Samarkand who sacked Damascus and Delhi.
question.clue: This man captured Sultan Bayezid the Thunderbolt at the Battle of Ankara.

swap.text: Along with many explorers before and after him, Ibn Battuta made use of this vast network of land and sea routes which linked Asia, Europe, and Africa.
swap.clue: A 2015 best-selling history book by Peter Frankopan is titled for the plural form of this entity.

question.text: The heqin policy was later revived by the Tang when Princess Wencheng ("win-chung") was sent to marry this region's king Songtsen Gampo. A monastery in this Himalayan region's capital of Lhasa was built to house a Buddha statue she supposedly brought.
question.answerHtml: Tibet [or Bod or Xizang; accept Tibetan Empire or Tufan or Tubo]
question.clue: A religious leader from this country formerly ruled from the Potala Palace but now lives in exile in India.

swap.leadin: This country's golden Neutrality Monument of its first president once rotated to face the sun.
swap.text: Name this country, whose first president Saparmurat Niyazov instituted bizarre totalitarian laws such as renaming its calendar months and dates after himself and banning gold teeth.
swap.clue: The Rukhnama, or "Book of Soul," was a propaganda work written by a former head of this state, Saparmurat Niyazov.

question.text: This Central Asian proxy conflict between the British and Russian empires provided the justification for the war, as the British feared Dost Mohammad Khan would side with the Russians in a potential invasion of India.
question.clue: The Fortress of Orenburg was constructed in order to control the Kazakhs as part of this period, which also saw extended maneuvering over the rights to Sinkiang.

swap.leadin: This empire was formed in the 7th century AD following the end of the Zhangzhung kingdom.
swap.text: Name this ancient Himalayan empire which flourished until the 9th century and had a capital at Lhasa.
swap.clue: Ralpacan was one of this empire's Three Dharma Kings.

question.leadin: A faction of bandits led by Habibullah Kalakani in this country was named the Saqqawists, deriving from his nickname as the son of a water carrier.
question.text: Name this modern-day country whose emirate was once ruled by the Durrani family. William Elphinstone led a British retreat from this country.
question.clue: In 1977 Loya Jirga secured one party rule under the National Revolutionary Party under a President who was the cousin of former king Mohammad Zahir Shah.

swap.text: This republic on the Yenisey near Mongolia was independent, with its capital at Kyzyl, from 1921 to 1944.
swap.clue: Under Chinese rule from 1757 to 1911, Russia helped it achieve independence in 1911 and annexed it in 1944.

question.text: The European Union suspended most diplomatic relations with Uzbekistan following the May 2005 incident in this city, where demonstrators were massacred by the army in Bobur Square after twenty-three accused terrorists broke out of prison.

swap.text: Islamist forces countering the Soviets were known by this term, which can refer to Muslim guerilla fighters.
swap.clue: A manual titled for the "victory" of people known by this word prescribed 200 men to fill each "cushoon" operating rocket artillery in Tipu Sultan's Mysorean army.

question.text: The Ballad of Mulan instead depicts her fighting the Rouran ("roh-rahn"), who are the first historical people of note to use this title for their rulers. This Turkic title was also given to the leader of the Mongols.
question.clue: One of these figures destroyed the Khwarezmian cities of Urgench and Samarkand and established his capital at Karakorum.

swap.leadin: A vizier of an empire whose capital was this city may have been a secret Manichaean.
swap.text: Name this city, the capital of the Samanid Empire whose rulers commissioned Ferdowsi to write the Shahnameh. Alongside the Khanate of Khiva, an emirate ruled from this city later became a Russian protectorate.
swap.clue: A group modelled off the Young Turks invited the Soviet conquest of this city and was given prominent leadership positions in the short-lived Soviet republic centered on this city.

question.text: This so-called "Stalin of Mongolia" sought to reunite Outer and Inner Mongolia, but was thwarted by the real Stalin. He served as leader of Mongolia from 1939 to 1952.
question.clue: With Shtern and Zukhov, this man commanded the winning side at the Battle of Khalkin Gol.

swap.text: The Afghan side at Panipat was led by this ruler, who had previously invaded India as a general of Nader Shah. This ruler united the Pashtun tribes to form the first modern Afghan state under the Durrani dynasty.
swap.answerHtml: Ahmad Shah Durrani [accept Ahmad Shah Abdali; prompt on Shah Durrani or Shah Abdali alone]
swap.clue: This cavalry commander discovered the leader of the Afsharid kingdom assassinated in a tent, prompting him to abscond with the royal seal and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

question.text: The author of History of the Hind, al-Biruni, traveled to India with the invading forces of Mahmud-i Zabuli, the first Sultan of this Turkic empire which broke off from the Samanids.
question.answerHtml: the Ghaznavid Empire [or Ghaznaviyan; Mahmud’s father Sabuktigin founded the dynasty but Mahmud was the first to call it a Sultanate]
question.clue: This empire whose first leader, Sabuktigin, was a slave before being promoted by Alptigin.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about operations during World War II that were never executed.
swap.text: The Nazis' capture of Paris uncovered secret plans for Operation Pike, which would have bombed cities in this mountain range. The Nazis' own Operation Edelweiss ("ED-el-vice") attempted to secure oil fields surrounding this range.
swap.clue: Gold and silver tubes, possibly used to drink beer, that were found in this region were made by the Maykop culture, which, like this region's Kura-Araxes culture, constructed burial mounds called kurgans.

question.leadin: They conquered their namesake city after Alp Tigin was dismissed from office and used his slaves to take it over.
question.text: Identify this Islamic dynasty based out of Afghanistan that brought Islam to the heart of India under their greatest ruler Mahmud.
question.clue: One of the dynasties that sprung up in Transoxiana after the demise of the Abbasids was this one, whose founder Sabuktigin founded it by seizing Samanid territory. Its sultan Mahmud patronized the poet Ferdowsi.

swap.text: In response to Olzhas Suleimenov's "Nevada" movement, Nazarbayev closed this Kazakh nuclear facility in 1991. This facility's namesake city on the Irtysh River suffered from increased birth defects and cancer rates as a result of the 456 nuclear tests conducted there, including the very first Soviet test in 1947. It is also known by a geometric name.
